# michi

TypeScript/JavaScript bindings for [`michi`](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) — AXI response primitives for agent-ergonomic tools. Native binary via NAPI-RS: no WASM, no JS reimplementation of the rendering logic.

## Install

```bash
npm i @orin-dx/michi
```

npm installs the matching prebuilt binary as an optional dependency; see [Supported platforms](#supported-platforms).

## Quick start

```typescript
import { renderToon } from "@orin-dx/michi";

const out = renderToon({
  typeName: "issues",
  fields: ["number", "title", "state"],
  rows: [
    [
      { type: "int", intVal: 51815 },
      { type: "str", strVal: "[Bug]: Telegram plugin" },
      { type: "str", strVal: "open" },
    ],
    [
      { type: "int", intVal: 51812 },
      { type: "str", strVal: "dark mode request" },
      { type: "str", strVal: "open" },
    ],
  ],
  totalCount: 8771,
  hints: ["Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue"],
});

process.stdout.write(out);
```

```text
issues[2]{number,title,state}:
  51815,"[Bug]: Telegram plugin",open
  51812,dark mode request,open
totalCount: 8771
help[1]: Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue
```

## API

Every string these functions return for an agent is a TOON 4.4 document with no trailing newline — lists, key-value blocks, errors, status, recovery hints and help blocks alike.

### Free functions

| Function | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `renderToon` | `(opts: ToonOptions) => string` — TOON list rendering |
| `emptyState` | `(typeName: string) => string` — definitive empty-state block |
| `emptyStateWithHints` | `(typeName: string, hints: string[]) => string` — the empty-state block plus `help[N]: …`; like `emptyState`, throws `toon_validation_failed: …` for a `totalCount`/`help`/`recovery` type name |
| `renderHints` | `(hints: string[]) => string` — the inline array `help[N]: h1,h2` |
| `appendHints` | `(body: string, hints: string[]) => string` — append `help[N]: …` to a document, on its own line |
| `renderRecovery` | `(hints: RecoveryHint[]) => string` — the table `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` (`params` is `"{}"` here; an absent reason is `null`) |
| `renderKv` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number, hints: string[]) => string` — `key: value` lines; throws `kv_validation_failed: …` for a repeated key or a `totalCount`/`help`/`recovery` key |
| `renderDomainError` | `(code, message, hints, githubAnnotation?, causes?) => string` — `error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`, `help` |
| `renderStatus` | `(toolName, description, items, hints?) => string` — `tool`, `description`, the table `items[N]{key,value,health,reason}:`, `help` |
| `renderAlreadyDone` | `(operation, summary, hints) => string` — `operation`, `status: already_done`, `summary`, `help` |
| `alreadyDone` | `(stored?: string \| null) => { done: boolean, result?: string }` — classify an idempotency lookup: any stored string (even empty) is done |
| `renderPartialSuccess` | `(completed: OpRef[], failed: FailedOp[], skipped: OpRef[]) => string` — the summary, the `completed[N]{index,operation}:`, `failed[N]{index,operation,reason}:` and `skipped[N]{index,operation,reason}:` tables (`index` is the op's position in your batch; a skipped op's `reason` is a machine token, `null` when absent) and the failed ops' `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` table |
| `renderPipeline` | `(steps: PipelineStep[]) => string` — the table `step[N]{id,name,status,reason}:`; `status` is a `StepStatus` label (`completed`, `outcome_unknown`, …) and `reason` is required exactly for `outcome_unknown`, `skipped` and `not_run` |
| `truncate` | `(content: string, maxChars: number) => { content, originalChars, removed, wasTruncated }` — text that fits comes back unchanged; a longer text keeps its first `maxChars - 1` chars and ends in `…`, and the cut is reported in `removed` and `wasTruncated`, never inside `content`. Add your own hint, for example `cut ${removed} of ${originalChars} chars; pass full=true`, to the response's `help[]`. |
| `parseRetryAfter` | `(headerValue: string) => number \| null` — an RFC 9110 `Retry-After` value (delay-seconds or HTTP-date) in seconds; a past date is `0`, a malformed value `null` |
| `nextRetryDelay` | `(maxRetries, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitterFactor, jitterSeed, attempt, retryAfterMs?) => number \| null` — the next back-off delay in ms, or `null` once retries are used up; pass a random `jitterSeed` in `[0, 1]` per call |
| `isRetryableStatus` | `(status: number) => boolean` — `true` for 429, 502, 503 and 504; retry 502 and 504 only for idempotent requests |

### `AgentResponse` class

The primary integration point — a builder that composes TOON/KV rendering, hints, and recovery into one response.

Setters return `void`, not `this`, so call them as sequential statements rather than a chain. (Chaining isn't supported across the NAPI boundary — see `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md` in the main repo for why.)

| Method | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `(typeName: string)` |
| `.items` | `(rows: ToonValue[][], fields: string[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a TOON list section named for the response's type; each call adds one, rendered in call order. `totalCount` is how many rows existed before a cut and renders only when it is larger than the rows passed |
| `.kvItems` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a key-value section the same way |
| `.hint` | `(hint: string) => void` |
| `.recoveryHint` | `(tool: string, reason?: string) => void` |
| `.truncationHint` | `(hint: string) => void` — the caller's instruction for getting a cut cell in full (same as `ToonOptions.truncationHint`). Cut cells end in `…` and are listed in a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block; when a cell was cut, the hint adds one `help[]` line after your own hints. Without it the block still reports each cut |
| `.asError` | `() => void` |
| `.renderText` | `() => string` — the sections in call order, then `help[]` and `recovery[]` |
| `.renderJson` | `() => string` — compact JSON: `{"body":...,"sections":[...],"hints":[...],"recovery":[...],"isError":bool}` |
| `.renderHintsOnly` | `() => string` — just the `help[N]: …` line |
| `.humanContent` | `(text: string) => void` — attach a `user`-audience companion block for `toCallToolResult()` |
| `.hasHumanContent` | `() => boolean` — whether `.humanContent()` was set |
| `.renderFor` | `(audience: "assistant" \| "user") => string` — `"user"` returns the `humanContent` block if set, otherwise the assistant rendering |
| `.toCallToolResult` | `() => CallToolResult` — the MCP `tools/call` response shape: `{content, isError, structuredContent}`, with each content block's `annotations.audience` set correctly |

Full type definitions ship in `index.d.ts`. See the [main repo](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) for the complete primitive set, the TOON grammar, and the `michi-core` Rust API this wraps (this package always carries the same version as `michi-core`).

## Supported platforms

Prebuilt native binaries ship for:

- macOS on Apple silicon (`darwin-arm64`, package `@orin-dx/michi-darwin-arm64`)
- macOS on Intel (`darwin-x64`, package `@orin-dx/michi-darwin-x64`)
- Linux x64 with glibc (`linux-x64-gnu`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-x64-gnu`)
- Linux x64 with musl (`linux-x64-musl`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-x64-musl`)
- Linux arm64 with glibc (`linux-arm64-gnu`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-arm64-gnu`)
- Linux arm64 with musl (`linux-arm64-musl`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-arm64-musl`)

Windows isn't supported yet. Building from source needs a Rust toolchain (see [`rust-toolchain.toml`](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/blob/main/rust-toolchain.toml) in the main repo).

## License

FSL-1.1-MIT — Functional Source License, converting to MIT two years after each release. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

content.content:
180:- has leading or trailing whitespace (space or tab),
181:- is exactly `true`, `false` or `null`,
182:- looks numeric: `/^[+-]?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:e[+-]?[0-9]+)?$/i` — `42`, `-3.14`, `05`, `+1`, `1e-6`,
183:- contains `:`, `"`, `\`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, a comma, or any control character U+0000–U+001F,
184:- starts with `-` or `#`.
185:
186:Everything else — Unicode, emoji, interior spaces, `|`, `<`, `=` — stays bare. Inside quotes, `\` and `"` are escaped as `\\` and `\"`, LF, CR and tab as `\n`, `\r` and `\t`, other control characters as `\u00xx` with lowercase hex; nothing else is escaped. A cell or hint therefore never spans lines and nothing is dropped. A cut cell is quoted by the same rules after the cut.
187:
188:## Trust model
189:
190:michi guarantees a syntactic property and nothing more.
191:
192:**What michi guarantees.** One value cannot create extra lines, fields or cells. A line break, tab or any other C0 control in a value is escaped (`\n`, `\t`, `\u00xx`), and a comma, colon, quote, bracket or leading `-` forces quotes, so a cell stays one cell of one row. Text inside a cell therefore cannot produce michi's own lines either: `truncated[…]`, `totalCount`, `help[…]`, `recovery[…]`, `causes[…]` and `error:` are written by michi, from structure the caller supplied, and a cell that spells one of them stays a quoted cell.
193:
194:**What michi does not do.**
195:
196:- It cannot stop prompt injection. A cell is still text the agent reads; "ignore previous instructions" inside a cell is rendered faithfully, as data.
197:- It escapes only C0 controls, as TOON 4.4 §7.1 specifies. C1 controls (U+0080 to U+009F), U+2028 and U+2029, bidirectional controls and tag characters (U+E0000 block) pass through verbatim.
198:- `audience` annotations on MCP content are advisory metadata for the client, not access control.
199:- Truncation cuts on `char` boundaries, not grapheme clusters, so it can split a multi-part emoji or a flag pair. The output is valid UTF-8 and cannot panic, but the cut character may render oddly.

lines: Any `#[napi]` function returning `napi::Result<T>` throws a JS `Error` on `Err`. Two practices apply here:

-- Wrap fallible conversions (row shape mismatches, oversized inputs) in `Result` and surface them as `napi::Error::from_reason(...)`. Inputs that cannot form a valid TOON document throw with a prefixed message: `toon_validation_failed: …` from `renderToon`, `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` (a reserved `typeName`), `kv_validation_failed: …` from `renderKv` (a duplicate key, or a reserved `totalCount`/`help`/`recovery` key). `renderPipeline` throws for a status or reason that does not name a `StepStatus` (`unknown step status "done": expected one of pending, …`, `step status "skipped" needs a reason: prerequisite_failed or cancelled`, `step status "completed" takes no reason, got "timeout"`).

Inputs that cannot form a valid TOON document throw with a prefixed message: `toon_validation_failed: …` from `renderToon`, `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` (a reserved `typeName`), `kv_validation_failed: …` from `renderKv` (a duplicate key, or a reserved root key such as `help` or `message`; the list is in [02](02-toon-format.md#trust-model)). `renderPipeline` throws for a status or reason that does not name a `StepStatus` (`unknown step status "done": expected one of pending, …`, `step status "skipped" needs a reason: prerequisite_failed or cancelled`, `step status "completed" takes no reason, got "timeout"`).
- Annotate exports that call into non-trivial rendering with `#[napi(catch_unwind)]`.
- Without it: **a Rust panic crashes the entire Node process** — there's no isolation boundary.
- With it: a panic becomes a thrown JS `Error` (or a rejected `Promise` for async) instead of process death.

michi renders a budget; it never computes one. Which items survive a budget is the caller's decision — a BM25 cutoff, a reserved-floor allocator, monokl's `apply_budget` degrade-then-drop ladder. Reporting what got cut in a consistent agent-readable shape is the part every caller needs identically, which is exactly the split [`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md) describes for truncation.

136:Absent fields are omitted rather than rendered as `null`. The roll-up renders only when the response carries two or more sections. A single-section response already states its count in its own TOON header and `totalCount:` line, and repeating it costs tokens for nothing. michi writes the roll-up from the response's own sections when it renders (name, count, total, derived `truncated`), so it can name no section the response lacks and cannot disagree with the `totalCount` lines above it. # Decisions

This file tracks open questions and API-shape rationale. Workspace-level decisions are indexed in [`docs/adr/`](../adr/README.md); current behavior is specified in the relevant API reference.

## Open questions

Tracked by what they block, not by sequence number — "Q1/Q2/Q3" reads too easily as calendar quarters, which these aren't.

### Resolved 2026-10-23 — TOON keeps retrieval accuracy

Measured on Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol (94 questions × 5 formats × 3 repeats each): TOON is within noise of pretty and minified JSON, Markdown-KV and a Markdown table on every model, at the lowest token cost, so TOON stays the default for assistant-facing lists. Untested: Gemini and open-weight models, lists much longer than 100 rows, open-ended tasks. Details and limits are in the [research note](../research/toon-retrieval-accuracy.md).

### Open until two consumers agree — measurement-basis rendering

**Blocks:** a shared rendering primitive for measured and modeled values

ProjectAtlas distinguishes observed values, deterministic derivations, and modeled counterfactuals. Lumen may need the same distinction. This supports investigation, not a new Michi domain type.

First test whether the proposed `ProvenanceBlock` and ordinary section fields express this clearly; see [the envelope proposal](07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md). Add a `MeasurementBasis`/`Measured<T>` API only when two real consumers need the same wire contract and the design passes the five gates in `PRINCIPLES.md`. Michi renders the basis; callers decide whether a value is observed, derived, or modeled.

This question adds no production dependency. External telemetry or TOON crates remain evaluation/dev dependencies unless an implementation spec proves otherwise.

### Deferred to v2 — `cli` feature scope

**Blocks:** terminal-aware rendering

Reserved for terminal-aware rendering.

- If `--format toon` in a human terminal context should wrap long rows or colourize the header, this is where that lives — likely a `render_terminal()` variant consulting terminal width (`crossterm`) and applying ANSI colour to health signals and the type header.
- Out of scope for v1: michi v1 targets agent consumers only, not human-readable terminal output.

cat >> docs/spec/06-decisions.md <<'EOF'

### Resolved 2026-11-16 — Envelope facts have one source

The architecture and security audits of 0.10.0 rendered documents that contradicted themselves: a section with `totalCount: 5` and `"truncated": false`, a budget roll-up naming a `ghost` section beside two real ones, a success response whose KV items read exactly like a `DomainError` (`error:`, `message:`, `exit_code:`), and a provenance label posing as the fingerprint. Each came from a fact the caller supplied twice or a key list kept in three places. The envelope is unstable (ADR 10), so this is the window to close them. It amends "Public types can grow" for `Section`, and supersedes the `returned_count`, roll-up and root-key bullets of "Envelope implementation deviations" and the `truncated_section` bullet of "One section model".

- **`Section` fields are private.** Read them with `name()`, `body()`, `count()`, `total()` and `truncated()`. `count()` is the rows or items for `Toon` and `Kv`; a `Text` body carries the count its constructor was given (`Section::text` gives 1 for non-empty text, `Section::text_with_count` any number), so `SectionBody::Text` is now `Text { text, count }`. `truncated()` is derived, `total > count`, and there is no setter. `total_count(Option<usize>)` stays the one fact a caller sets. Rejected: a `Completeness { Complete, Cut { total: Option<usize> } }` enum for "cut, total unknown": no consumer reports a cut without a total, and the derived flag covers every case that renders.
- **`truncated_section` builds the section from the outcome.** It takes `(name, fields, &outcome, row, guidance)` and maps `outcome.kept` to rows itself, so the list's `[N]`, `totalCount`, the JSON `returnedCount`/`truncated` and `showing N of M` all describe one cut. The old form took a ready-made section beside the outcome, and five rows beside an outcome that kept two rendered both (its rustdoc claimed otherwise). Toon only: a cut KV or text section sets its own total and gets a self-consistent `truncated` the same way.
- **The budget roll-up is derived.** `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section` are removed. `sections[n]{name,returned,total,truncated}:` is written from the response's own sections at render time, still only with two or more. `BudgetSummary` keeps only what michi cannot know: ceilings, usage and `truncated`, now meaning "the budget dropped something the sections cannot show". The rendered `truncated` is that flag or any cut section, so `budget: truncated: false` cannot sit above a cut section. content.content:
## Releasing

[Callisto](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto) versions and publishes `michi-core`, `michi-pipeline`, `michi-graph` and `@orin-dx/michi`. They're a fixed group (`michi`), so a change to any of them releases all four on one version.

1. With your change, add a changeset: a Markdown file in `.changeset/` (any name, e.g. `.changeset/toon-quote-tabs.md`). The front matter maps each changed package to a bump (`major`, `minor`, `patch` or `none`); the body is the changelog entry, written for users of the package.

   ```markdown
   ---
   michi-core: patch
   ---

   `render_toon` quotes cells that contain a tab.
   ```

   Package names are `michi-core`, `michi-pipeline`, `michi-graph` and `michi-node` (the npm package). Changes with no user-facing effect don't need one.

2. Merging to `main` opens or updates Callisto's version PR (`callisto/version-packages`), which bumps versions and writes the changelogs.
3. Merging the version PR runs the Release workflow (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`): it builds the native binaries, publishes to crates.io and npm, and creates one GitHub release tagged `michi@{version}`.

**Post-release check.** When the run published a package to a registry, or a re-run adopted one from a failed earlier attempt, the `smoke-published` job installs that version from the public registries into clean projects on Linux x64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64 and uses it: `npm install @orin-dx/michi`, render TOON, then build a program against `michi-core`, `michi-pipeline` and `michi-graph` from crates.io. It retries for up to 10 minutes while the registries catch up. It also fails if any of the seven npm packages lacks a provenance attestation (`SMOKE_REQUIRE_ATTESTATIONS=1`): `@orin-dx/michi` is published by pnpm and the platform packages by npm, and pnpm only reads `PNPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`, so releases through 0.7.1 shipped the main package unattested. A red job means the published packages are broken, so fix forward with a new release. Run the same check by hand with `just smoke-published <version>`.

The first publish of a brand-new npm package can fail with Callisto error E157: npm accepted the upload but doesn't show the version yet. That's registry propagation lag. Wait a few minutes, then use "Re-run failed jobs" on the Release run. It adopts what already landed and publishes the rest. Don't regenerate the release intent.

Each FSL-licensed published package carries a copy of the root `LICENSE` (`crates/michi-core/LICENSE`, `crates/michi-pipeline/LICENSE`, `packages/michi-node/LICENSE`, `packages/michi-node/npm/*/LICENSE`); `michi-graph` has its own MIT `LICENSE`. If the root license changes, copy it to each; `crates/michi-core/tests/license_copies.rs` fails until they match.

## Commit Style

Use imperative conventional commit prefixes: `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `ci:`.

michi-core: `AgentResponse` keeps its body in one list of sections. `items()` and `kv_items()` are shorthand that append a section named for the response's type, so calling both renders both bodies in call order instead of silently dropping one, as long as their root keys differ. Every section is a root key of the document: a repeated key (two `items()` calls, two `kv_items()` with a shared key, a name like `budget`, a repeated provenance label) renders the `toon_validation_failed` error naming the key, with `isError` true, instead of invalid TOON. For several lists use `.section(Section::toon(distinct_name, ..))`. The same applies to `@orin-dx/michi`'s `items()` and `kvItems()`, which render one list per response. A `Text` section now renders as one escaped string value (`name: "..."`), not raw prose.

gh pr create --draft --base main --head refactor/envelope-integrity --title "refactor(core)!: give every envelope fact one source" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What

Envelope integrity (trail T1). Every fact a response reports about itself now has one source:

- `Section` fields are private (getters `name`, `body`, `count`, `total`, `truncated`). `truncated` is derived (`total > count`), never set. `SectionBody::Text` is `Text { text, count }`; `Section::text_with_count` replaces the `returned_count` setter.
- `truncated_section(name, fields, &outcome, row, guidance)` builds the rows from `outcome.kept`, so `[N]`, `totalCount`, the JSON counts and `showing N of M` cannot disagree. The old rustdoc promise was false.
- The budget roll-up is derived from the response's sections. `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section` are gone. Budget `truncated` renders true when any section was cut. The budget JSON loses its `sections` array.
- One reserved-root-key list (`toon::RESERVED_ROOT_KEYS`) for `ToonDocument::validate`, `render_kv` and the collision check. It now includes `budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `error`, `message`, `causes` and `exit_code`. `fingerprint` is always a reserved provenance label.
- A private `json` module and a `toon::table` writer replace the duplicated JSON helpers and table headers.
- The `include_str!` source-grep tests are gone. Replacements: trybuild cases (`toon_options_new_must_use`, `section_facts_are_derived`), a `list` call with each string type, and `debug_assert*` in `.clippy.toml` `disallowed-macros`.

Rendered text is unchanged apart from the listed reserved-key errors. All 8 insta snapshots pass untouched.

## Why

Audit findings architecture #1, #2, #7; security #6, #7; duplication #2, #3, #5, #11 (the hand-typed `SectionCost` part), #8; rust-perf #4. The decision is recorded in `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`, under "Envelope facts have one source".

## How checked

- `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust` (1130 passed), `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` (1152 passed), `just typos`, `just check` (includes doc-check, fuzz-check, deny, zizmor and md fmt): all exit 0.
- `pnpm build && pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node`: exit 0 (158 pass).
- `scripts/check-api-docs.py origin/main HEAD`: exit 0.
- New probe tests in `tests/envelope_integrity.rs` cover the audits' bad states (`totalCount:5` with `truncated:false`, the `ghost,99` roll-up, the forged error document, the forged fingerprint). Each failed on main before the fix.
- 12 mutants were run, and each was caught by a test, trybuild or clippy.

## Not run

Release-mode tests and the fuzz targets themselves (the targets build).

## Decisions

- The budget's `truncated` is the caller's flag OR any cut section.
- `causes` is reserved along with `error`, `message` and `exit_code`.
- `status.rs` and `pipeline/mod.rs` still write their own table headers. They are outside this trail and can move to `toon::table` later.
- Minimal edits outside the trail: the `napi.rs` tests and 4 doc lines (the reserved-key message and list), one line in `packages/michi-node/__test__/index.test.mjs`, `empty.rs` (it now uses the shared list), and `lib.rs` (the `mod json` line and the `SectionCost` re-export).
EOF

input.message:
Draft PR for T1 (envelope integrity): https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/pull/122, branch `refactor/envelope-integrity`. I did not merge or force-push.

**Findings**
- **Fixed:** architecture #1, #2 and #7; security #6 and #7; duplication #2, #3 and #8; the `SectionCost` part of duplication #5; rust-perf #4.
- **Not done:** duplication #11. The positional hints/`totalCount` parameters belong to a later trail.
- **Not moved:** `status.rs` and `pipeline/mod.rs` still write their own table headers. Both are outside this trail.

**API changes the later trails build on**
- **`Section` fields are private.** Read them with `name()`, `body()`, `count()`, `total()` and `truncated()`. `truncated()` is derived from total versus count and has no setter.
- **Text sections:** `SectionBody::Text` is now `Text { text, count }`, and `Section::text_with_count` replaces the `returned_count` setter.
- **`truncated_section(name, fields, &outcome, row, guidance)`** builds the rows from `outcome.kept`.
- **Budget:** `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section` are removed, and the roll-up is derived from the sections. The budget's rendered `truncated` is the caller's flag or any cut section. Its JSON no longer has a `sections` array.
- **Shared code:** one reserved-key list, `toon::RESERVED_ROOT_KEYS` (11 keys, `causes` added as my own decision). New internal `json` module and `toon::table` writer. `ToonDocument::render_list` replaces `render_parts`.

**Checks (all exit 0):** `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features`, `just typos`, `just check`, `scripts/check-api-docs.py`, and `pnpm build && pnpm test`. Release-mode tests and actually running the fuzz targets were not done.

**Mutants:** 12 deliberate faults, every one caught by a test, a compile-fail case or clippy.

**Edits in other trails' files:** `napi.rs` (tests plus 4 doc lines), one line in `index.test.mjs`, `empty.rs`, `lib.rs` and `.clippy.toml` (new `debug_assert` ban). T2 will need to carry the `napi.rs` lines over when it splits that file.

**Surprises:** `pnpm test` rewrites `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and `just check` rewrites a stale `fuzz/Cargo.lock`. I reverted all three.
